title: Rain window
suits: focus, reading, writing, music, cafés and cities, remote work, 'the quiet hour': you are inside, looking out. The name goes on the glass. Not for sunny or high-energy pitches.

params.data-tod: 0…1, the hour: 0 blue hour, 0.5 evening, 1 late night (fewer cars, the last tram nearly empty, stronger reflections)
params.data-word: the café's name in gold leaf on the glass, read backwards from inside (any length, it shrinks to fit). use-pack --word fills it; default 'Café'
params.data-seed: integer; reshuffles the buildings, the lit windows and the rain
params.data-print-t: clock time of the still frame for print (default 26.5: the tram is passing)
params.--brand on the section: optional: the neon sign across the street and its reflection on the wet road take --brand

details: every drop on the glass is a lens: it shows a patch of the street behind it, upside down
drops cling until rain landing on them feeds them past a size; then they run, catch on the glass, pause, and run again (stick-slip)
a running drop swallows every drop it touches and grows, and wipes a clean path through the mist of tiny droplets
it leaves a trail of small beads behind it, and new rain slowly mists the path over again
the glass is warmed up with 23 s of simulated rain before the first frame, so the first look is already lived-in
the headline corner gets fewer drops and less mist, so the type sits on calm glass
condensation is on the inside of the pane, thick along the bottom and in the corners; now and then a bead forms in it and runs down to the sill, clearing a line that fogs over again
the café's pendant lamps and its name in mirrored gold leaf are reflected in the glass, stronger the darker it gets outside
the street is painted, then blurred like a wide-open lens; lamps and lights stay round as bokeh with brighter rims
the wet road smears the shopfronts and lamps into long reflections
rain is visible outside only where a street lamp lights it
the traffic light down the street cycles red 12 s, green 10 s, amber 3 s, and its colour runs down the wet road
the pharmacy cross blinks its pattern: on, on, off
headlights pass one way on the near lane, tail lights the other, each trailing a streak across the wet road; fewer late at night
a tram glides past every 52 s with passengers in its lit windows and a blue spark at the wire; late at night it is the last one, nearly empty
passers-by under umbrellas bob with each step against the shop light
steam curls off the coffee on the sill; a bead of water sits where the glass meets the wood; a small plant trails one strand over its pot
